summary.text: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II) burned solid fuel samples in a small flow duct aboard the International Space Station, in the Microgravity Science Glovebox. The cited result is the opposed-flow velocity at which flames over thin PMMA sheets extinguished, and how that velocity changed with reduced O2.

fuels.text: PMMA fuel samples, 20 mm wide and about 95 mm long, with thickness ranging from 100 to 400 µm, in the extinction-velocity tests.

geometry.text: A 76-mm square duct with PMMA samples burned in an opposed-flow configuration.

oxygen.text: The O2 level can be adjusted to 21 percent or below.

flow.text: Flow velocity can range from 0 to 50 cm/s.

gravity.text: Microgravity combustion tests performed aboard the International Space Station.

measurements.text: Flames were photographed with a high-resolution digital still camera at a frame rate of 1 per second, and a radiometer was used to confirm flame extinction.

claims.text: The investigation aims to study the ignition, flame growth, flame spread, and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows in microgravity.
The investigation hypothesizes that materials in microgravity, with adequate ventilation, burn as well if not better than the same material in normal gravity.

In opposed-flow tests of PMMA samples, extinction velocities were found to be about 1 cm/s for thicknesses of 100, 200, and 300 µm and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 µm. The source describes a second test in which flow was gradually reduced. The fan voltage at extinction indicated a flow velocity of about 1.1 cm/s.

Tests were also conducted at a lower O2 level of about 16 percent for two thicknesses. The extinction velocities were found to be about 2.6 cm/s for 100 µm and about 4 cm/s for 200 µm. The source states that the extinction velocity significantly increases as the O2 level is reduced.

Measured extinction flow velocities and their dependence on O2 level are candidate inputs to the combustion computational models that the source says are used in designing fire detection and suppression systems in microgravity and on Earth.

conditions.text: PMMA samples 100 to 400 µm thick, 20 mm wide and about 95 mm long, burned in opposed flow in a 76-mm square duct aboard the ISS; flow was gradually reduced until the flame extinguished.
Opposed-flow tests on PMMA samples at a lower O2 level of about 16 percent, aboard the ISS. The samples were 100-µm and 200-µm thick; sample widths differed between thicknesses.

limitations.text: The source states there are significant uncertainties in the low extinction velocity values because calibration at such low velocity has high error bars.
The lower-O2 data are limited: the source notes insufficient data at the lower O2 level, and sample width differed between thicknesses tested (20 mm for 100 µm, 10 mm for 200 µm).
The space-based extinction results come from a limited number of tests.

modeling_resources.description: Experimental table of BASS-II run records that may hold run conditions for the opposed-flow PMMA tests; its contents were not examined for this card.

extinguishes at about 30 s after ignition. The fan voltage at that time indicates a flow velocity of about
